model_output.score_comment_short: The projects show relevant tools, while most teaching bullets describe responsibilities.
model_output.score_comment_long: The housing capstone and student dashboard show analytics work in two different settings. Most experience bullets stop before explaining how you approached the data or what you found. Adding those details to a few existing bullets would make the transition easier to assess.
model_output.score_plain: Your resume shows a basis for an analytics transition, but it leaves readers with questions about how you work through an analysis. More detail in the projects and teaching examples would help them assess your fit for a data role.
model_output.first_impression: Your move from mathematics teaching into data analytics is immediately clear. The student dashboard is worth keeping prominent because the math department used it to decide which units needed re-teaching.
model_output.biggest_gap_example: "Analyzed student assessment data to identify learning gaps and adjust instruction" does not show what you found or changed, leaving the analysis itself hard to assess.
model_output.summary: Your analytics transition draws on classroom assessment work and a housing affordability capstone using Python and SQL. You also built an Excel dashboard around AP Statistics pass rates and quiz scores, connecting data work to a department decision. Your titles show an experienced teacher, while the projects introduce your work with analytics tools. The housing project doesn't yet say what you found, so a reader has little to judge about your interpretation of the data.
strengths: Teaching Algebra II and AP Statistics to approximately 150 students per year across 6 class periods makes your classroom responsibilities concrete.
The housing capstone names 10 years of data and a Tableau dashboard by zip code, giving the project a defined subject and time range.
Mentoring 3 new teachers through the district induction program shows a responsibility beyond your own classes.
gaps: The housing project names a presentation but not the findings shared with instructors and peers, making its conclusions difficult to evaluate.
The assessment-data bullet doesn't give an example of an instructional adjustment, so the connection between analysis and teaching remains abstract.
The skills list includes several tools and methods, but it doesn't distinguish those demonstrated in the projects from those without an example on the resume.

top_fixes.fix: In the housing analysis bullets, add one finding you presented and explain how you compared housing and income data.
top_fixes.why: A reader can then see what your Python and SQL work helped you examine, rather than only the tools used.

evidence.excerpt: - Analyzed 10 years of Austin housing and income data using Python and SQL

top_fixes.fix: In the student assessment bullet, give one example of a learning gap you identified and the instructional adjustment you made.
top_fixes.why: That example would make your classroom analysis more tangible to a reader considering your move into analytics.

evidence.excerpt: - Analyzed student assessment data to identify learning gaps and adjust instruction

top_fixes.fix: In the student dashboard bullets, explain how you prepared the pass-rate or quiz-score data for the Excel dashboard.
top_fixes.why: The department's use of the dashboard is already stated; the preparation detail would show more of your analytical work.

evidence.excerpt: - Built an Excel dashboard tracking AP Statistics pass rates and quiz scores over three years

next_steps: Expand the housing capstone with a verified finding and the comparison behind it.
Revise the assessment and student dashboard bullets using examples from your actual work.
Review the summary and skills list against the revised projects, putting demonstrated analytics work before general claims.
